_: CAMP-56. The record of who read our legal pages before they went live. See scripts/seo/check-legal-review.mjs. While `acknowledgedUntil` is in the future a public build warns; past it, it fails. That is the same shape as known-advisories.json: a debt we have looked at, with a date it stops being acceptable.
jurisdiction: Belgium — Wetboek van economisch recht, plus GDPR and Directive 2011/83/EU. The company is UTD BV, Antwerpen.
reviewedBy: Claude (Anthropic), acting for the owner — NOT a lawyer. See `note`.
note:
WHAT THIS RECORD CLAIMS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.

Who read these pages. Not a lawyer. On 27.10.2026 the owner decided there would be no lawyer on this project — there is no budget for one — and that this review would be done by me. This record is not legal advice and does not replace it. It asserts exactly one thing: every statement on these pages was checked against the code, and wherever the two disagreed, the page or the code was changed.

What was checked, and how. On 02.11.2026 six pages were read for the first time and thirteen discrepancies were found between text and code; three more of the same kind turned up afterwards in places the first pass had not listed. All are closed. The pages no longer promise to accept photographs and reviews the code does not accept; no longer call one browser key the only one when there are three; no longer claim a tick-box confirming age that does not exist; no longer say "we hold the following, and nothing else" while listing what we do not hold. Each checked statement now has a test that turns red when the code and the text drift apart, and every one of those tests was proved by mutation.

WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM.
- That the wording is optimal under Belgian law. It is TRUE; that is a different thing.
- That the list of processors will stay complete. It is complete on this date and is held by a test.
- That Article 28 contracts exist with every processor. With Hetzner, yes, concluded 02.11.2026. With Cloudflare, NOT CHECKED — the register says so in those words.
- That the pages were checked against the national law of other member states, beyond what follows directly from the GDPR and Directive 2011/83/EU.

When this record stops applying. By itself, the moment any named page's version is raised: the guard compares versions, not names. That is deliberate — what was read was a specific text, not "the terms" in general.

Why the acknowledgement runs only three months. This review was done by a non-lawyer. Law moves, our reading of it ages, and a record that sits unquestioned for a year stops being a review and becomes a habit. Three months is short enough that somebody has to look again while the reasons for each decision are still recoverable from this repository.
